# Lemonade Design System — web tokens

CSS custom properties for Teya's Lemonade design system.
Import `@teya/lemonade-mobile-ds/tokens.css`, or paste `lemonade.css` into a <style> block.
Light theme is the default; dark applies automatically from the OS, or explicitly
with `data-lmnd-theme="dark"` on any element.

Always prefer a semantic token over a literal value.

## Colours

- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-brand)` — Use for primary brand surfaces, such as key actions or highlights.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-brand-elevated)` — Use for brand surfaces with subtle emphasis, such as secondary actions or accents.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-brand-high)` — Use for strong brand emphasis, such as headers, banners, or high-priority surfaces.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-brand-subtle)` — Use for elevated brand surfaces, such as cards or containers with brand emphasis.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-always-dark)` — Use for surfaces that must always appear dark, regardless of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-always-dark-high)` — Use for high-emphasis surfaces that must always appear dark, regardless of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-always-dark-low)` — Use for low-emphasis surfaces that must always appear dark, regardless of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-always-dark-medium)` — Use for medium-emphasis surfaces that must always appear dark, regardless of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-always-light)` — Use for surfaces that must always appear light, regardless of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-always-light-high)` — Use for high-emphasis surfaces that must always appear light, regardless of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-always-light-low)` — Use for low-emphasis surfaces that must always appear light, regardless of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-always-light-medium)` — Use for medium-emphasis surfaces that must always appear light, regardless of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-transparent)` — Use for transparent surfaces or when layering elements.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-transparent-dark)` — Use for transparent dark surfaces or when layering elements over lighter content.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-transparent-light)` — Use for transparent light surfaces or when layering elements over darker content.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-default-inverse)` — Use as the inverse of bg-default, typically for dark backgrounds.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-elevated-inverse)` — Use as the inverse of bg-elevated, for higher elevation on dark backgrounds.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-subtle-inverse)` — Use as the inverse of bg-subtle, for elevated surfaces on dark backgrounds.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-caution)` — Use for cautionary states, such as warnings or potential risks.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-caution-subtle)` — Use for subtle backgrounds indicating caution.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-critical)` — Use for critical states, such as destructive actions or errors.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-critical-subtle)` — Use for subtle backgrounds indicating critical context.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-featured)` — Use for featured states, such as highlighted or promoted content.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-featured-subtle)` — Use for subtle backgrounds indicating featured content.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-info)` — Use for informational states, such as system feedback or neutral alerts.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-info-subtle)` — Use for subtle backgrounds indicating information.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-neutral)` — Use for neutral states that don’t carry positive, caution, or critical meaning.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-neutral-subtle)` — Use for subtle backgrounds without strong semantic meaning.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-positive)` — Use for positive states, such as success messages or confirmations.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-positive-subtle)` — Use for subtle backgrounds indicating positivity or success.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-default)` — Use for the primary background of screens and surfaces.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-elevated)` — Use to create a higher elevation background against bg-default or bg-subtle.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-elevated-high)`
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-subtle)` — Use for secondary backgrounds, such as cards, containers, or inputs placed on bg-default.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-brand)` — Use for borders that reinforce brand identity or highlight key interactive elements.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-on-brand-high)` — Use for strong or high-contrast borders on brand surfaces.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-on-brand-low)` — Use for subtle borders placed on brand-coloured surfaces.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-on-brand-medium)` — Use for medium-emphasis borders on brand surfaces.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-always-dark)` — Use for borders that must always appear dark, regardless of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-always-dark-high)` — Use for strong dark borders that require high contrast or clear separation, independent of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-always-dark-low)` — Use for subtle dark borders that require minimal emphasis, regardless of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-always-dark-medium)` — Use for standard dark borders that need clear visibility in any theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-always-light)` — Use for borders that must always appear light, regardless of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-always-light-high)` — Use for strong light borders that require high contrast or clear separation, independent of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-always-light-low)` — Use for subtle light borders that require minimal emphasis, regardless of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-always-light-medium)` — Use for standard light borders that need clear visibility in any theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-brand-inverse)` — Use for brand borders on dark or inverted backgrounds.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-neutral-high-inverse)` — Use for standard borders on dark or inverted backgrounds.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-neutral-low-inverse)` — Use for subtle borders on dark or inverted backgrounds.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-neutral-medium-inverse)` — Use for standard borders on dark or inverted backgrounds.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-selected-inverse)` — Use to indicate selection or active state on dark or inverted backgrounds.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-caution)` — Use for borders that indicate warnings or potential risks.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-caution-subtle)` — Use for subtle borders that signal caution with low emphasis.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-critical)` — Use for borders that indicate errors or destructive actions.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-critical-subtle)` — Use for subtle borders related to error or destructive contexts.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-featured)` — Use for borders that indicate featured or highlighted content.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-featured-subtle)` — Use for subtle borders that convey featured or highlighted content.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-info)` — Use for borders that indicate informational or neutral states.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-info-subtle)` — Use for subtle borders that support informational messages.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-positive)` — Use for borders that indicate success or confirmation states.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-positive-subtle)` — Use for subtle borders that convey success or positive feedback.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-neutral-high)` — Use for high-contrast borders or strong dividers that require clear visual separation.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-neutral-low)` — Use for subtle dividers or low-emphasis element boundaries.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-neutral-medium)` — Use for standard borders and general element outlines.
- `var(--lmnd-color-border-selected)` — Use to indicate a selected or active state on components.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-brand)` — Use for brand-coloured text or icons to reinforce identity.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-brand-high)` — Use for brand-colored text or icons to reinforce identity.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-on-brand-high)` — Use for text/icons on high-emphasis brand backgrounds.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-on-brand-low)` — Use for text/icons on subtle or low-emphasis brand backgrounds.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-always-dark)` — Use for text or icons that must always appear dark, regardless of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-always-light)` — Use for text or icons that must always appear light, regardless of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-caution-always-on-color)` — A fixed foreground colour for text and icons placed on cautionary backgrounds, ensuring consistent visibility regardless of theme.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-critical-always-on-color)` — A fixed foreground colour for text and icons placed on critical or error backgrounds, ensuring consistent visibility regardless of theme.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-info-always-on-color)` — A fixed foreground colour for text and icons placed on informative backgrounds, ensuring consistent visibility regardless of theme.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-neutral-always-on-color)` — A fixed foreground colour for text and icons placed on neutral backgrounds, ensuring consistent visibility regardless of theme.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-positive-always-on-color)` — A fixed foreground colour for text and icons placed on positive or success backgrounds, ensuring consistent visibility regardless of theme.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-brand-inverse)` — Use for brand-coloured text/icons on dark backgrounds.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-primary-inverse)` — Use as the primary content colour on dark backgrounds.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-secondary-inverse)` — Use as the secondary content colour on dark backgrounds.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-tertiary-inverse)` — Use as the tertiary content colour on dark backgrounds.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-caution-on-color)` — A strong background used to signal warnings or cautionary states that require user attention without implying error.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-critical-on-color)` — A strong background used for critical messages, errors, or destructive actions that require high visibility.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-featured-on-color)` — A strong background used to highlight featured, premium, or promoted content that needs visual emphasis.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-info-on-color)` — A clear background used to present informative messages or neutral system states that guide the user.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-neutral-on-color)` — A neutral background used to present default or non-semantic content that carries no positive, caution, or critical meaning.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-positive-on-color)` — A strong background used to confirm success, completion, or positive feedback that needs visual emphasis.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-caution)` — Use for cautionary text/icons, such as warnings.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-critical)` — Use for critical text/icons, such as errors or destructive actions.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-featured)` — Use for featured text/icons, such as highlights or promoted content.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-info)` — Use for informational text/icons, such as neutral alerts.

- `var(--lmnd-color-content-positive)` — Use for positive text/icons, such as confirmations.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-primary)` — Use for main text, titles, and essential content.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-secondary)` — Use for secondary text, such as body copy or supporting content.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-tertiary)` — Use for tertiary text, such as metadata, placeholders, or helper text.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-always-dark-high-interactive)` — Use for interactive states on high-emphasis surfaces that must always appear dark, regardless of theme or mode.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-always-dark-low-interactive)` — Use for interactive states on low-emphasis surfaces that must always appear dark, regardless of theme or mode.

- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-settlement-business-days)` — Use as the background for the Business days settlement frequency.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-settlement-everyday)` — Use as the background for the Everyday settlement frequency.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-settlement-instant)` — Use as the background for the Instant settlement frequency.
- `var(--lmnd-color-bg-settlement-scheduled)` — Use as the background for the Scheduled settlement frequency.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-on-settlement-business-days)` — Use for text and icons on the Business days settlement background.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-on-settlement-everyday)` — Use for text and icons on the Everyday settlement background.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-on-settlement-instant)` — Use for text and icons on the Instant settlement background.
- `var(--lmnd-color-content-on-settlement-scheduled)` — Use for text and icons on the Scheduled settlement background.
- `var(--lmnd-color-shadow-default)`
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-amber-background)` — Generic amber surface. Use for application-defined meaning — charts, categories, states with no semantic token. Pair with on-background for the label.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-amber-background-high)` — High-emphasis generic amber surface, carrying more weight than background. Light goes deeper, dark goes lighter, so it stands out from the page in either theme. Pair with on-background-high.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-amber-border)` — Generic amber border. Use for application-defined meaning where no semantic token applies.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-amber-content)` — Generic amber text and icons on a default surface. Also legible on background-subtle.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-amber-content-inverse)` — Generic amber text and icons for a surface whose brightness is inverted relative to the theme — a dark surface in light mode, a light one in dark. The mode-swapped counterpart of content, which is tuned for the default surface and drops below AA on an inverted one.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-amber-on-background)` — Text and icons drawn on top of background. Uses the hue’s own lightest or darkest step where that meets contrast, otherwise white or ink — chosen per hue, do not substitute a fixed neutral.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-amber-on-background-high)` — Text and icons drawn on top of background-high. The hue's own far end from that fill — on-background is tuned for background and does not carry here.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-amber-subtle-background)` — Subtle generic amber surface. Pair with on-background for the label, optionally outlined with border.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-amber-subtle-border)` — Subtle generic amber border. Pairs with background.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-amber-subtle-on-background)` — Text and icons drawn on top of the subtle amber background. The hue's own content colour, which stays legible on a pale fill.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-blue-background)` — Generic blue surface. Use for application-defined meaning — charts, categories, states with no semantic token. Pair with on-background for the label.

- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-green-lime-on-background-high)` — Text and icons drawn on top of background-high. The hue's own far end from that fill — on-background is tuned for background and does not carry here.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-green-lime-subtle-background)` — Subtle generic green lime surface. Pair with on-background for the label, optionally outlined with border.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-green-lime-subtle-border)` — Subtle generic green lime border. Pairs with background.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-green-lime-subtle-on-background)` — Text and icons drawn on top of the subtle green lime background. The hue's own content colour, which stays legible on a pale fill.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-indigo-background)` — Generic indigo surface. Use for application-defined meaning — charts, categories, states with no semantic token. Pair with on-background for the label.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-indigo-background-high)` — High-emphasis generic indigo surface, carrying more weight than background. Light goes deeper, dark goes lighter, so it stands out from the page in either theme. Pair with on-background-high.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-indigo-border)` — Generic indigo border. Use for application-defined meaning where no semantic token applies.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-indigo-content)` — Generic indigo text and icons on a default surface. Also legible on background-subtle.
- `var(--lmnd-color-themed-indigo-content-inverse)` — Generic indigo text and icons for a surface whose brightness is inverted relative to the theme — a dark surface in light mode, a light one in dark. The mode-swapped counterpart of content, which is tuned for the default surface and drops below AA on an inverted one.

## Components

Every component is CSS plus markup. React is optional: the classes below are the API, so
any framework — or none — produces the same result.

With React: `import { Button } from '@teya/lemonade-mobile-ds/react'` and
`import '@teya/lemonade-mobile-ds/components.css'`.
Without React, write the markup and import the same stylesheet. `buttonClasses` from the
root export builds the class list for you in any TypeScript stack.

### Button

```html
<button
  type="button"
  class="lmnd-button lmnd-button--primary lmnd-button--solid lmnd-button--large lmnd-text-body-medium-semibold"
>
  <span class="lmnd-icon" style="--lmnd-icon: url('.../icons/plus.svg')"></span>
  <span class="lmnd-button__label">Add item</span>
</button>
```

- Block: `lmnd-button`. Always pair it with one variant, one size and the size's text style.
- Variant: `lmnd-button--primary`, `--secondary`, `--neutral`, `--critical`, `--on-brand`, `--on-color`.
- Type: `lmnd-button--solid`, `--subtle`, `--ghost`. Omit it for `--on-brand` and `--on-color`,
  which carry a single treatment.
- Size: `lmnd-button--x-small`, `--small`, `--medium`, `--large`.
- Text style: `lmnd-text-body-small-semibold` for x-small and small,
  `lmnd-text-body-medium-semibold` for medium and large.
- Label: wrap it in `lmnd-button__label`.
- Disabled: the DOM `disabled` attribute. Do not add a class.
- Loading: add `lmnd-button--loading`, replace the label with
  `<span class="lmnd-button__spinner" aria-hidden="true"></span>`, drop the icons, and set
  `disabled` and `aria-busy="true"` plus `aria-label` so the button keeps its name.
- Full width: set the width on the element. Add `lmnd-button--expand` to stretch the label
  area and leave the icons at the edges.

Hover and press come from the stylesheet; do not add classes for them.
